subject: Clarification: IP & Training Rights in Order Form / MSA
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@kilntech.com>

Cc: Markus Berg <mberg@kilntech.com>, Legal Ops <legal@kilntech.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on IP / Training language in MSA and Order Form

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — KilnTech is excited about the potential for using Redwood for our customer support summarization pipeline. Legal flagged a couple of things in the redlined Order Form / MSA we just sent back (attached). Two core items they asked us to get clarity on:

1) Output ownership. The current Order Form says "Customer is granted ownership of Outputs" but the MSA includes a broad license back to Redwood for "service improvement." Legal wants to confirm that KilnTech will retain ownership of model outputs (generated content) and that any Redwood use of those outputs for model training or product improvements requires explicit opt-in.

2) Training / data use. KilnTech cannot agree to any clause that allows provider training on customer data by default. We requested a carve-out: Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for monitoring/bug fixes, but not for model training or deploying customer data into training sets unless KilnTech opts in via a separate agreement.

3) Feedback license. We suggested limiting any license to non-exclusive, non-commercial use for providing/operating the service, and allowing Redwood to derive aggregated statistics but not retain or repurpose raw customer prompts/outputs.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on the three points above, and whether you can accept the redlines in the attached Order Form? If you have proposed alternative language, please send it over so our counsel can review. We would like to keep the procurement timeline this week if possible.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

Best,
Samantha Li
Director, Strategic Programs
KilnTech

Attachments: KilnTech_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx

Subject: Re: Questions on IP / Training language in MSA and Order Form

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in our legal (Laura) and product (Maya) to propose workable language. High-level position from Redwood:

- Customer outputs: We are comfortable with Customers retaining ownership of Outputs they generate. We typically grant a limited license back to Redwood to the extent necessary to provide the Service (e.g., to store and deliver outputs to the Customer). We do not want a broad perpetual assignment.

- Training / data use: Redwood’s default policy is NOT to train models on customer-specific prompts/outputs unless customer explicitly opts in. We can accept a clause that prohibits using Customer Data or Outputs to train models, with an exception for de-identified, aggregated telemetry used for safety and reliability monitoring. We can also offer a paid opt-in program for customers who want their data to be used to improve models (explicit written consent, separate SOW).

- Feedback license: We can accept a narrow feedback license for: (i) using de-identified and aggregated feedback to improve the service; and (ii) performing internal analytics. We will not retain or repurpose raw prompts/outputs for commercial model training without an opt-in.

Laura — can you please propose redline snippets (short, trackable edits) I can send to Samantha? Maya — FYI on the opt-in train-for-features product path; happy to discuss pricing/track. Samantha — I’ll aim to get proposed language over by EOD Pacific and a short explanation of the operational safeguards (retention, access controls, deletion upon request).

Quick ask on timing: if we can get legal view + agreement to the language today, I can route final signatures to DocuSign tomorrow and keep the integration kickoff on schedule.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Questions on IP / Training language in MSA and Order Form

Thanks for the ping — below are suggested redline snippets and negotiating rationale. I kept the language tight so it can be inserted into the MSA and Order Form without expanding scope.

1) Outputs ownership — proposed language to add to Order Form (or MSA section titled "Customer Materials / Outputs"):

"Customer Outputs. Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated by the Service using Customer Input. Provider (Redwood Inference) is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to store, cache, and display Customer Outputs solely to provide the Service to Customer and to perform any support or maintenance activities requested by Customer. Provider shall not claim ownership of Customer Outputs."

Rationale: preserves Customer ownership while giving Redwood the operational license needed to render & deliver outputs.

2) Training / model improvement — proposed MSA clause:

"Use of Customer Data for Model Training. Provider will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or improve Provider models or machine learning systems except (a) with Customer's prior written consent executed by an authorized representative, or (b) as necessary to provide de-identified, aggregated analytics and telemetry for the sole purpose of monitoring, debugging, or improving the availability/performance of the Service. De-identification shall be performed in a manner intended to prevent re-identification and Provider shall document techniques used upon Customer request."

Rationale: This prohibits training on raw customer data while allowing limited safe telemetry use. We can offer an addendum for paid opt-ins.

3) Feedback license — proposed language to be added to MSA:

"Feedback License. Customer grants Provider a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Customer Feedback for the purpose of improving the Service and related offerings, provided that such Feedback is de-identified and aggregated and not reasonably capable of re-identification. Provider will not use Customer Feedback that contains Customer Proprietary Data or Outputs for commercial model training without Customer's express written consent."

Notes / operational controls:
- Retention: propose a default telemetry retention window (e.g., 90 days) for customer-level raw logs unless longer retention is requested.
- Access controls: restrict access to raw customer data to a small operations/security team; production models/datasets used for training must not include raw customer data unless opt-in SOW executed.
- Auditability: we can provide an attestation / summary of de-identification techniques upon request; SOC2 controls apply.

I attach a PDF with highlighted redlines you can send to Samantha. If Procurement pushes back on retention window, we can offer a short-term extension or a secure, on-request export/deletion feature in the private deployment.

Happy to join a call with KilnTech counsel if needed; otherwise send Samantha the proposed language and I will stand by for any follow-ups.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on IP / Training language in MSA and Order Form — proposed language

Samantha — thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review, please find our proposed inline language below (you can copy/paste into the redline doc):

1) "Customer Outputs" — Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs. Provider is granted a limited license to store, cache, and display Outputs to deliver the Service. Provider will not claim ownership of Outputs.

2) "Use of Customer Data for Model Training" — Provider will not use Customer Data or Outputs for training or model improvement except (a) with Customer's prior written consent executed by an authorized representative, or (b) to the extent necessary to generate de-identified, aggregated telemetry used solely for monitoring, debugging, or improving service reliability. De-identification techniques will be documented upon request.

3) "Feedback License" — Customer grants Provider a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use de-identified and aggregated Feedback to improve the Service. Provider will not use Feedback that includes Customer Proprietary Data or Outputs for commercial model training without Customer's express written consent.

Operational items we will commit to:
- Default telemetry retention window: 90 days for raw logs; aggregated summaries retained longer for product analytics.
- Access limits: raw customer data (where present) will be accessible only to a restricted ops/security group.
- Opt-in program: we offer a paid opt-in for customers who want Provider to include Customer Data/Outputs in product training; this will be covered by a separate SOW and consent.

Next steps I propose:
- If KilnTech legal is comfortable with the language above, Laura can incorporate tracked changes into the MSA and Order Form this afternoon.
- I will then route to our commercial signatory and prepare a DocuSign packet.
- We can also schedule a 30-minute call if you prefer to walk counsel through the de-identification / security controls.

DocuSign (proposed package will be ready after Laura inserts final tracked changes): https://docusign.example.com/packages/KD-2026-87
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/KD-2026-87

Samantha — let me know if any of this is a deal-breaker. We want to preserve KilnTech's ownership while keeping the door open for a clear opt-in path for model training.

Thanks,
